body.statement: Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\). If \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=\varepsilon_{q,n}=\delta_n=n^{-1/8}\), then eventually \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), \(b_n(\alpha/16)=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), \(\rho_n(\alpha/16)=O(n^{-1/2})\), \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}=O(n^{-3/4})\), \(d_n\asymp d_n^-\asymp n^{-1/4}\), \(s_n\asymp B_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\), and \((L_G(C_n^*),L_N(C_n^*))=(O(n^{-1/4}),O(n^{-3/8}))\). If \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=0\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then \(\Lambda_n=1\), \(d_n^-=d_n=B_n=n^{-1/2}\), and no rate shortening occurs.
body.justification: The reductions verify a genuine gain and the perfect-treatment-fit benchmark.
body.gap: No comparator reports these shrinking-cumulant calculations for one union-honest interval.
body.consumer: They give calibrated simulation and software checks.
